items.reason: The passage identifies the intended captive as the man of God but does not state that he came from Judah, as the expected answer specifies.
Micah directly identifies his mother as the person who uttered the curse concerning the stolen silver.
The passage explicitly says they decided to go to the Syrian camp, but the expected answer adds surrender, an intention not directly stated in this excerpt.
Verse 7:15 explicitly says the road was strewn with clothing and equipment.
The Danites explicitly ask the Levite to inquire whether their journey will be successful.
The passage identifies Sceva’s seven sons as the exorcists and directly describes them fleeing wounded after being overpowered.
The prophet explicitly addresses the man of God from Judah when announcing that his body will not enter his ancestors’ tomb.
The passage lists an ephod, household gods, and one silver-covered image. The expected answer instead lists a graven image and a separate molten idol, which this passage does not support.
Micah explicitly gives the Levite becoming his priest as his reason for expecting the Lord to be good to him.

The question does not distinguish the burning from other killings in Shechem. The passage describes burning a temple stronghold containing people from the tower, not explicitly killing Shechem’s leaders by burning the tower.
